  "summary": "S1 [fact] The target is the existing dependency-free Node.js help-desk service, with src/server.js, PORT-based npm start and a bin/ CLI; discovery should inspect README.md, package metadata, source, CLI and tests as leads, not verified contents. S2 [fact] Add ticket assignment within that service. S3 [fact] PUT /tickets/:id/assignee accepts a JSON assignee that is null or a non-empty name of at most 64 characters; discovery resolves existing response and error conventions (Q4–Q5). S4 [fact] Only open and in-progress tickets may be assigned or unassigned; discovery establishes their existing representations (Q5). S5 [fact] Reassigning to the current agent changes nothing; the recorded default also sends no notification for that no-op (Q6). S6 [fact] Every ticket exposes assignee, null when unassigned; discovery establishes existing state lifetime, sharing and access rules (Q7). S7 [fact] The assigned agent must be notified; discovery first checks runtime identity and notification facilities (Q1), and a person must specify a channel if none is available (Q2), which blocks completion of notification only. S8 [fact] GET /tickets filters by an assignee name or, for an empty value, unassigned tickets, combined with every other supplied filter; discovery establishes current filter conventions (Q4, Q13). S9 [fact] The CLI listing displays each assignee; discovery establishes its current format (Q4). S10 [fact] Existing service behavior and unchanged existing tests must continue to work; discovery identifies their coverage and risks (Q3, Q13). S11 [fact] Add node:test coverage under test/ and run it with the existing suite through npm test; discovery inspects the harness (Q10). [assumption] API clients, CLI users and assigned agents are the consumers; the request establishes no new interactive UI, authentication, private per-user state, session lifetime or state-ending event, so existing runtime behavior governs those matters and no new identity or privacy system is implied (Q1, Q7). [assumption] No prior-run continuation, deployment target, named team, workspace, channel, internal site, private repository or owner is specified; discovery may use repository references as unverified leads and must keep any sensitive locator in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. [boundary] Intake implements nothing and grants delivery to the existing service checkout; during an isolated run the source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when the outcome becomes visible there. A deployed outcome would be visible only after release, which this request does not specify."
